lead: Two robots, Perseverance and Curiosity, are working on Mars today. This page shows what time it is where they are, which Mars day they are on, and how long a radio message takes to reach them. Your device works it all out; no internet data needed.
try: Look at the two rover clocks under What time is it on Mars? Then, under How far away is Mars?, press Next opposition, then Next conjunction, then Play.
points: A Mars day, called a sol, is 24 hours, 39 minutes and 35 seconds long. Each rover counts its sols from the day it landed.
Mars is between about 55 and 400 million kilometres away, so a message takes from about 3 to 22 minutes to get there. Nothing can travel faster than light.
About every two years the Sun gets between Earth and Mars. Then NASA stops sending commands to the rovers for about two weeks.
